info.name: Document Extraction Local API
info.description:
Use this collection for the Document Extraction Workspace API.

Prerequisites:
1) Run bun run build && bun run start from the repository root.
2) Configure the Workspace model gateway in the browser.
3) Generate a Workspace API key.
4) Set api_key and template_id, or use template_tags for automatic selection.
5) Select one upload example and attach a PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP.

Workspace settings control Smart splitting. With splitting enabled, PDF uploads return packet_id. Other uploads return job_id. Upload scripts save poll_path from Location. Poll the submission, then read each child_job_ids entry with Return Job Results.

The API preserves packet identity even when the frontend presents one document. All product endpoints require Bearer API-key authentication. See mkdocs/docs/api/overview.md for the full specification.

request.description:
Create a template. Omit field IDs and object column keys. The API derives IDs from field names and column keys from headings.

Expect HTTP 201 with { template_id, version, status }.

Update a template. Omit field IDs and object column keys. The API derives IDs from field names and column keys from headings.

Expect HTTP 200 with { template_id, version, status }.

Select this example or 1b and attach document. Expect HTTP 202, Location, and job_id or packet_id. Smart splitting also applies to PDFs with an explicit template. All children inherit that template version. The script clears stale IDs and saves poll_path for Check Submission Status. Repeating an upload creates new work.

request.description: As an alternative to 1a, omit template_id and send a nonempty JSON array of tag names. Candidates match ANY supplied tag. Each split child selects independently. Unknown tags match nothing and can require manual selection. Workspace settings control Smart splitting. The script saves job_id or packet_id and poll_path. Repeating an upload creates new work.

request.description:
Poll the saved Location, normally every 2–5 seconds. Job states are queued, processing, awaiting_template, completed, and failed. Packet states are queued, processing, awaiting_review, materializing, processing_children, completed, and failed.

A signed-in Workspace member resolves template or boundary holds in Documents before processing continues. Packet reads include child summaries without results. The script saves child_job_ids. Copy each required ID to job_id and use Return Job Results. Record consumed IDs in your integration to prevent duplicate imports. A failed packet can still contain successful or running children.

Read an ordinary job or one packet child. For packets, set job_id to each child_job_ids value in turn. Completed jobs include results. Other states return results: []. Failed jobs return HTTP 200 with error_code/error_message. For awaiting_template, a signed-in Workspace member selects a template in Documents. This example expects a completed job.

exec: pm.test('Job should be completed for full results', function () {

request.description: Read the parent and current children with the packet_id saved during upload. Children include job_id, status, parent_packet_id, and source_pages from the original PDF. Read each child job for extracted fields. A completed all-blank packet has outcome no_documents and no children.
Read effective enable_smart_splitting and exclude_blank_pages settings. Owners and admins change these settings in the browser. Each accepted upload records its effective settings.
Download an available retained source or working source held for review. A child source contains only its assigned pages. Source errors do not change extraction results.
Download the full original when retained or available for review. It includes excluded pages and pages from deleted children.
